unit.why: The Komarno rebbe reports that his uncle and master, R. Zvi Hirsh, told him how he was expelled in disgrace from Brody on a Friday and then received a wondrous illumination in prayer.

stories.start_quote: עוד בס׳ זוהר חי הנ"ל בזה"ל
stories.summary_en: R. Zvi Hirsh tells his nephew-disciple that he still fears the kelipat nogah. He recounts being driven in disgrace out of Brody on a Friday, arriving home in Podkamin without Sabbath clothes, and then praying for light and feeling all his limbs ignite during prayer; the narrator adds that he habitually drew suffering on himself each Friday to receive divine light on the Sabbath.

quotes: עדיין הייתי מפחד האם אני חלילה בקליפת נוגה
עדיין בכל עת ורגע אני מפחד מזה
tags.why: He constantly fears being under the kelipat nogah.

quotes: גורש משם בעש"ק בבזיון גדול ונורא
tags.why: He is publicly humiliated by the expulsion.
He is expelled from Brody, presumably by opponents.

quotes: ולא הי׳ לו בגדי שבת עד אחר התפלה
tags.why: The events are framed by Friday and the Sabbath.

אן גיצונדען מאנע איברים בעת התפלה
tags.why: His prayer and the experience during it are central.

tags.why: He receives divine light in rapt prayer.

tags.why: He describes a unique mystical experience in prayer.

quotes: והמשיך על עצמו יסורין ודוחק וצער בכל עש״ק
tags.why: He habitually took suffering on himself each Friday.

quotes: ואמר לי הקדוש מורי ורבי דודי
tags.why: The intimate teaching exchange between master and disciple frames the story.
The tale illustrates the tzaddik's holy conduct and fear of sin.
The master is the narrator's uncle, which is extended family only.
